title: An accepted result stops being current after the covered tree changes
description: A result was accepted for a covered tree. Afterwards a file under the covered tree changes. The correct behavior is that the acceptance is no longer presented as current, and no exit is claimed without fresh evidence.

oracle.judges: Compares the digest the acceptance was recorded for against the recomputed covered digest, and whether the system still presents the acceptance as current.

expected.claim: An acceptance is current only while the covered tree still matches the digest it was recorded for.

shared.task_inputs: task.md and fixtures/ are byte-identical for both variants.
shared.frozen_check: fixtures/check.sh, frozen before any variant runs.

divergent.evidence_acquisition: The baseline has no recorded acceptance digest and can only notice the change by re-running. The exitbind variant compares the recorded acceptance digest against the current one. The oracle judges the currency relation itself.

threats_to_validity: A system that re-runs everything on every read also satisfies this scenario, so the scenario does not distinguish 'detects drift' from 'never trusts anything'; that is intentional and recorded as a limitation.
The covered tree boundary is declared by the fixture; a product with a different boundary notion is not judged against it here.
